feature: 9.8.1 / Table 120 common descriptor fields and use
title: Descriptor is shared by simple fonts and CIDFonts; required fields and glyph-space metrics
source_location: ISO/EC3 primary PDF: printed pp.343–345 (physical pp.358–360); Markdown doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8340–8385. §9.8.1/Table 120 is printed page 343 onward; footer checked in spec-layout.txt.
errata: EC3 #190 amends Descent to <= 0 and adds a NOTE that source font metrics may use either sign; PDF expects negative. #474 makes FontWeight 1..=1000 a shall and the nine hundreds a should. #152 changes FontWeight's type from number to integer. #453 (listed by errata-read.md under §9.8.2) amends MissingWidth predictability: use is predictable only when uncovered codes' glyph widths all match; otherwise behavior is implementation-dependent.
ledger: Rows §9.8 and §9.8.1 at doc/conformance/ledger.toml:2635, 2643. The broad row describes descriptor metrics, fallback, and Type0 exclusion. It discusses #190/#474/#152 but does not name #453; the row's simple statement that MissingWidth defaults to zero should be qualified by #453 when describing predictable outcomes.
code: pdf-font::metrics::missing_width reads the value or defaults zero; simple_widths uses it for uncovered codes. vertical_extent reads Ascent/Descent only when both are finite and plausible, else uses the documented em-box policy. loading::opening resolves descriptors for simple fonts and CIDFont descendants; Type0's outer dictionary is not treated as a descriptor. A missing descriptor becomes NotEmbedded/substitution rather than a reader rejection.
tests: metrics.rs::missing_width_tests checks explicit and absent default; declared_range_tests checks LastChar controls; metrics.rs measured_extent/vertical_extent tests cover accepted and implausible pairs; selection_geometry and text-state audit tests check public selection consequences. `unreadable_program_substitute` and `silent_fonts` exercise missing/unusable programs. These are not tests of mandatory reader rejection for a missing/malformed producer-required descriptor field.
assertions: Assertions establish deterministic defaults and the bounded selection-band policy, not rejection of producer-invalid entries. A missing descriptor for non-standard fonts is tolerated through substitution. EC3 #453 makes the inconsistent-width case implementation-dependent, so the current fixed width choice is not an ISO defect. #152/#474 change writer validity; reading real-number or out-of-range FontWeight values permissively is not itself a reader violation.
verdict: core consumer paths evidenced; producer-validity requirements must remain distinct from reader duties
residuals: Ledger explanation should explicitly map #453 to the MissingWidth feature. No public regression presently isolates #453's valid predictable case (all uncovered codes same actual width) from its implementation-dependent inconsistent case; a reader is not required to reject the latter. This pass did not repeat the prior Ascent/Descent oracle review or audit every Table 120 entry's substitution usefulness. No test draft: the core MissingWidth cases already have independent direct assertions, and a new test should target exact glyphs whose widths are independently known before asserting #453's precondition.

title: Unsigned 32-bit word, Symbolic decision, advisory/producer constraints, and ForceBold
source_location: ISO/EC3 primary PDF: §9.8.2 printed pp.345–346 (physical pp.360–361); Table 121 and following prose at printed pp.345–347. doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8387–8440.
errata: EC3 #453 concerns MissingWidth's Table 120 text, not the meaning of Flags. Table 121's Symbolic/Nonsymbolic mutually-exclusive sentence and reserved bits are PDF-writer constraints. The processor should always check Symbolic. ForceBold says the processor shall determine whether bold glyphs shall receive extra pixels, then permits thickening at small sizes; actual thickening is not an unconditional shall.
ledger: §9.8.2 at doc/conformance/ledger.toml:2651. Claim that descriptor_flags maps invalid signed/over-wide values to no flags is directly test-backed. Claim that Symbolic alone controls the binary state matches the source's explicit 'should'.
code: pdf-font::metrics::descriptor_flags accepts only nonnegative u32-valued PDF integers; all invalid/missing values become zero. truetype::is_symbolic reads bit 3, and the TrueType code table ignores Encoding when symbolic. substitute::Style/family_of consumes Italic, ForceBold, FixedPitch, Serif, Nonsymbolic; ForceBold raises substitution weight to at least bold. No code raster-thickens embedded bold outlines.
tests: metrics.rs::flag_tests tests bit 3, bit 6, all-one word, negative, overwide and real. name_keyed.rs tests Symbolic has no effect for an embedded name-keyed program. silent_fonts.rs::a_descriptor_setting_both_symbol_flags_is_named_as_the_cause uses a real corpus fixture and checks the public report; rich_text and archive tests check invalid word handling. substitute.rs has separate family/italic/weight tests.
assertions: Evidence covers both direct bit reads and meaningful effects. `issue20232.pdf` is producer-invalid because both Symbolic and Nonsymbolic are set; the report names that conflict while the reader follows the source's Symbolic-priority recommendation. Reserved-bit validation is writer-only. Lack of small-device thickening is within the may clause; substitution choice uses the bit but is explicitly a permitted strategy.
verdict: selected reader behaviors are represented and assertions are meaningful; no confirmed mandatory reader gap
residuals: No dedicated public pixel test contrasts embedded TrueType Symbolic versus Nonsymbolic with differing Encoding/cmap results in this shard. Existing low-level tests and corpus conflict report cover the decisions, so this is a coverage refinement candidate, not a claimed defect. Unset-both is a producer violation and the should rule resolves it as non-symbolic; the reader need not reject or diagnose it.

title: Style, Lang, FD and deprecated CIDSet are CIDFont-only additions
source_location: ISO/EC3 primary PDF: printed pp.347–349 (physical pp.362–364); Table 122 and §9.8.3.2–.3.3. Markdown doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:8462–8505.
errata: EC3 #5 corrects §9.8.3.3's contradictory FD sentence: a class descriptor's keys are a subset of Table 120's metrics, while FontFile* and Table 122 CIDFont-specific entries are excluded. The source Table 123 adds Adobe-KR in PDF 2.0 and marks Adobe-Japan2 and Adobe-Korea1 deprecated in PDF 2.0; the code retains compatibility rows and includes KR.
ledger: §9.8.3/.1/.2/.3 at doc/conformance/ledger.toml:2659–2683. Ledger rows map Style/Panose to substitution, Lang to Identity-ordering script sampling, and FD class overrides to substitution; CIDSet is treated as non-decisive. EC3 #5 and the 2020 Adobe-KR addition are represented in the detailed §9.8.3.3 note.
code: substitute::panose reads /Style/Panose; substituted::script_sample reads /Lang where collection order does not specify script; loading::class_faces applies per-class descriptors using glyph_class::Decision; substitute::overridden only carries the relevant style inputs/metric values. glyph_class::tabulated contains Adobe-GB1/CNS1/Japan1/Japan2/Korea1/KR rows. CIDSet is not used to select/draw glyphs.
tests: panose.rs checks classification and substitute effects; substituted.rs tests Lang language selection for Identity ordering; loading.rs tests class-specific descriptor choice and disjoint classes, while glyph_class.rs tests ambiguous/unlisted/form-only classes and the specification example. Corpus test identifies a descriptor's forbidden Table-120 keys but is not a reader-rejection test.
assertions: Existing internal assertion bodies establish the relevant choice and class application. Reader substitution and `/FD` are a capability choice enabled by the descriptor-information clause, not a mandatory rejection policy for bad producer fields. EC3 #5 changes allowed writer keys; silently ignoring unsupported overrides is not established as reader nonconformance.
verdict: sampled paths align with source and errata; no demonstrated reader defect
residuals: The corpus has no non-embedded real-world /Lang case; the direct Identity-ordering test is the witness. Adobe-KR's Table 123 class set appears in code, but no public PDF integration test specifically exercises that newly added row. CIDSet deprecated in PDF 2.0 and no CIDSet membership/stream parsing test was reviewed. No blanket certification of each class key or every override is intended.
